caveat petition.definition: Precautionary petition lodged under Section 148A CPC praying that no ex-parte interim order be passed without giving prior notice to caveator

prima facie.definition: Evidence sufficient on its face to establish a fact or raise a presumption of law unless disproved

mala fide.definition: Action taken in bad faith, dishonesty, or with unlawful motive to cause harm or wrongful gain

bona fide.definition: Action taken in good faith, honestly, and without fraud or malice

habeas corpus.definition: Prerogative writ commanding person or police detaining another to produce detainee before court to examine legality of detention

mandamus.definition: Prerogative writ directing a public authority or government official to perform a mandatory statutory duty

certiorari.definition: Prerogative writ quashing an illegal order passed by a lower court, tribunal, or quasi-judicial body in excess of jurisdiction

quo warranto.definition: Prerogative writ challenging the legal authority or qualification of a person holding a public office

prohibition.definition: Prerogative writ issued to an inferior tribunal preventing it from usurping or exceeding its statutory jurisdiction
